seoTitle: Google Ads for Pet Groomers: Setup, Budget, Keywords
description: How pet and dog groomers can run Google Ads: setup steps, keywords, realistic budgets, common mistakes, Local Services Ads and city-specific guides.
intro: This guide gathers our articles on Google Ads for pet groomers, including dog groomers, cat groomers, boarding facilities and daycares. It covers setup, keyword choices, budgets, common mistakes, Local Services Ads and city-specific guides for many US metro areas. It is meant for groomers who want more booked appointments from people searching nearby and are unsure where to begin.

If money is tight, read the step-by-step guide and the budget article first. Then use the keyword lists to build one tight campaign aimed at your service area, and read the mistakes articles before you launch. Start small, check search terms weekly, and make sure your Google Business Profile and booking page are ready, since ads send people there. Explore the city guides afterward.

Many groomers can launch a simple search campaign themselves, and the guides here are written for that. Consider help if you have spent a few months without bookings, your tracking is unclear, or managing ads cuts into grooming time. DataLatte offers Google Ads management for local businesses, but it is worth trying the basics first.

faq.q: How much should a pet groomer spend on Google Ads?
faq.a: It varies with your city, competition and how many appointments you can handle. Many groomers begin with a modest monthly test budget and increase it once ads clearly produce bookings. Our budget article walks through how to estimate a sensible figure for your situation.

faq.q: Are Google Local Services Ads available for pet groomers?
faq.a: Availability depends on your location and the categories Google currently supports, and it changes over time. Our Local Services Ads article explains how they differ from regular search ads and what to check before applying. Confirm current eligibility inside your Google account.

faq.q: What keywords should a dog groomer bid on?
faq.a: Start with high-intent local searches, such as dog grooming near me and grooming for specific breeds or services you actually offer. Add negative keywords to block job seekers and do-it-yourself searches. Our keyword lists give starting points you can adapt to your area.

faq.q: Why are my Google Ads getting clicks but no bookings?
faq.a: Common causes are broad keywords, a landing page that is hard to use on a phone, or no easy way to book. Check your search terms report and call tracking first. The mistakes articles cover these problems and how to fix them.
